main_text.p: feruare maximè oportet: qui grato animo aliorum agnoscere adhortationes debèt.

Sumendæ igitur hîc sententiæ erunt ex tri-Sententiæ rè bus locis: caufis, adiunctis, effectis: & o-sponsionum stendendum: pondus apud nos magnumad literas exhortatorias. exhortationem amici habuiffe: effeciffe illud: vt nihil in votis habeamus magis, quàm eidem fatis nos facere poffe. Propo- fita habere illam cómoda, & multa, & magna: laudem, honorem, opes, &c. effe honeftam quoq;, æquam, iuftam: prudentiæ & fidei plenam. Tum coluiffe nos & obferuaffe ab ineunte ætate amicum: propter paternam necefsitudinem, amorem noftri fingularem: prudentiam, autoritatem, promerita deniq; & plurima & maxima: ideoq; neq; iam fine reprehenfione graui ab eius nos difcrepare monitis pofe. Motus hîc duo locum habent: αἰχύνη[?] παθητικὰ[?] ἀρἀρ-gumenta. pudor feu verecundia, & ἐλπὶς[?] fpes, quę ex citatur argumenta. ... cùm fcilicet promittimus nosstudiosè diligenterq; facturos ea, quæ à nobis amicus requirit. Conciliantes ve-ἰδ̀ἀ argu-menta. rò fententiæ funt, quę laudem & commen dationem, gratiarum actionem, grati ani- mi pollicitationem, petitionem habent.
Fauemus enim iis, qui adhortationibus locum relinquunt: qui earúdem & fidem,

page.notes: The Greek words in the text and margin (αἰχύνη, παθητικὰ, ἐλπὶς, ἀρ, ἰδ̀ἀ) are only partly legible on the scan and are marked [?]. The printed margin reads "ἀρ" and "gumenta" as a word split across lines ("argumenta"); the first margin note sequence is read as printed. The "citatur" line has a Greek word (ζωγράφος-like form, printed "ζωγρίσε") and an ellipsis-like gap that is not transcribed as text. A small stray mark under the text on the page centre is not printed text and is omitted. The margin note "Sententiæ rè" is read with uncertainty.
